checks.diagnosis: The prompt allows cuts that separate a predicate from its sentence‑final inflection (tense/negation/politeness), producing contradictory or unusable fragments.
checks.evidence: ja_jp_1071, ja_jp_362, ja_jp_1294, ja_jp_1577, ja_jp_1034, ja_jp_999 — each policy cut left the verb or final auxiliary on the following piece and the measurement shows a high contradiction or fatal loss when that fragment is presented alone.
checks.type_predicate: Sentences where the main clause’s completing predicate (the sentence‑final verb or auxiliary sequence that supplies tense/aspect/negation/politeness) occurs later in the sentence than the candidate cut.

edit.text: Do not cut so that a verb stem or clause is left without its sentence‑final inflection; avoid cuts that separate a predicate from its finishing inflection (tense/aspect/negation/politeness).

orders.diagnosis: When several cuts all fall before the same sentence‑final inflection, the prompt fails to choose which is least harmful: the later cut (closer to the inflection) preserves more of the predicate and is preferable.
orders.evidence: ja_jp_1034, ja_jp_1071, ja_jp_362, ja_jp_1294 — in each sentence the target kept a later cut (closer to the finishing inflection) while the policy chose an earlier one that left more predicate behind, and the later cut yields much higher H_set.
orders.type_predicate: Sentences in which two or more candidate cuts occur inside the same clause immediately before the same sentence‑final predicate inflection (so both would leave the same verb unfinished).

edit.text: When multiple candidates fall before the same sentence‑final inflection, prefer the later cut (closer to the inflection) so the emitted piece preserves more of the predicate.
